name: Squad
tagline: AI assistant for product teams that turns rough ideas into structured strategy artifacts: opportunity maps, user stories, roadmaps and specs.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Underneath the framing, this is a structured prompt library plus a document store plus a tracker sync. An agent can absolutely build you a local workspace that takes a messy idea, walks it through discovery frameworks, and spits out opportunity trees, user stories and a PRD in markdown, and the output quality will be roughly whatever model you point it at. What you will not get in one sitting is the two-way Jira or Linear sync, the shared team workspace where a PM and three engineers argue in the same doc, or the opinionated method scaffolding that stops the LLM from producing generic slop. Solo operators and consultants who just need artifacts to think with are well served by the DIY build. Teams that need the artifacts to live where the work lives are not.
coreLoopDIY: Takes a one-paragraph product idea and generates linked, editable strategy artifacts (opportunity tree, user stories, acceptance criteria, PRD) stored locally as markdown with version history.
requirements: An LLM API key (OpenAI, Anthropic or a local model via Ollama)
Node 20+ and a local dev environment
Willingness to write your own framework prompts if you want output that is not generic
whatYouLose: Two-way sync with Jira, Linear or Azure DevOps, so your stories stay in a folder instead of the backlog
Real-time multiplayer editing and comment threads for the rest of the product team
Curated method scaffolding: their prompts encode a point of view about discovery, yours will encode whatever you typed at 1am
Hosted access for non-technical stakeholders who will not run a local server
Ongoing model and template updates you did not have to think about
moatNotes: The defensible part is not the generation, it is landing generated artifacts cleanly inside the tracker a team already lives in.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the artifact is not the point, the alignment is. A PM pays for this so a designer, two engineers and a skeptical exec can look at the same opportunity tree and the same acceptance criteria without a file being emailed around, and so the resulting stories appear in the backlog rather than in someone's Downloads folder. A local generator solves the blank-page problem, which is real, but the blank page was never the expensive part of product work.
notes: Great as a thinking tool for one person, thin as a coordination tool for five.
prompt:
Build a local-first product strategy workspace called "Crew". No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Next.js 15 (App Router) with TypeScript and Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3 for metadata and version history
- Markdown files on disk under ./workspace as the source of truth
- LLM calls through a single provider module; read OPENAI_API_KEY from .env.local, model configurable via env

Core loop:
1. User creates a Project with a name and a free-text problem statement.
2. From the project page, user generates artifacts in sequence. Each artifact type is a server action that sends a typed prompt template plus the project context to the LLM and streams the result:
   - Opportunity tree (desired outcome, opportunities, sub-opportunities, candidate solutions) rendered as nested lists
   - Assumption and risk list with a suggested test for each
   - User stories with acceptance criteria in Given/When/Then form
   - One-page PRD assembled from the artifacts above
3. Every artifact is editable in a plain markdown editor. Saving writes the file and inserts a row into a versions table with a timestamp and a diff summary.
4. Artifacts reference their parent artifact so later generations get earlier ones as context automatically.

Also include:
- Prompt templates stored as editable markdown files under ./prompts so the method can be changed without touching code
- Export: a button that zips the project folder, and a "copy as Linear issues" action that renders stories as a pasteable markdown checklist
- A projects index with search over titles and body text using SQLite FTS5

Out of scope: auth, multiplayer, real Jira or Linear API integration, comments, mobile layout beyond basic responsive, hosting.

Deliver a README with setup steps, an .env.local.example, and seed one example project so the UI is not empty on first run.
